title: bearings went just under warranty -  mfr replaced
text:
bearings went just under warranty - mfr replaced. I have been using the Norpro manual meat grinder for years now and was very satisfied with it. However, like all grinders it takes considerable time to clean. Since I could not do much of a quantity with my little Norpro I felt the ground meat output to clean up time ratio could stand some improving. So I looked for an inexpensive grinder that could do a larger quantity thereby making clean up time worthwhile.

This fits the bill. I knew going in it was not terribly powerful but I am not putting up mass quantities of ground beef or grinding up a deer or anything like that. It worked fine on a mix of chuck, sirloin and round. I did between 2-3 pounds which is about two weeks' worth for me. That would have been a good amount of grinding by hand.

Clean up is somewhat more complicated than the Norpro and this (and scant directions especially concerning "kubbe" sausage? attachments) are why I took off a star. Aluminum is lightweight and won't rust but it is a pain to clean when dealing with raw meat in that you cannot use a bleach solution on it. So it takes a lot of soaking/scrubbing in very hot soapy water. The mostly plastic Norpro can be cleaned with bleach ensuring that you are doing a good job sanitizing it. Of course grinder plate and blade needs to be hardened steel but I wouldn't mind a plastic hopper or chute.

Speaking of blade, whoever says this or any grinder won't grind at all almost certainly has the blade in the wrong way. It seems illogical when you have it facing against the grate but that is the proper way for any grinder to work.

UPDATE - the bearings (what it sounds like) have apparently gone after about 20 uses in 11 months. I have used this for 11 months as I said before, every 2-3 (lately more like 4) weeks. It is such a pain to clean (ALL grinders are) that I try to do a quantity of a couple pounds a time since I will be cleaning for at least an hour or two. I am NOT grinding Bambi's mommy. I am grinding cubed sirloin, round and chuck. Anyhow, after a session two weeks or so ago that went alright, today I cubed about 4 pounds of sirloin, chuck and round in preparation to grind. I assembled grinder and put some meat in hopper. IMMEDIATELY hear a horrible knocking sound and after a minute or two there was a smoky smell. I thought I had assembled something wrong so took it all apart with raw chunks of meat and put it back together, turned on the switch and same loud KNOCKING. OK, took off the whole hopper assembly and grinder, nothing but the motor and sure enough switch it on and the knocking and smoke. OK, it is the motor, probably bearings. This thing was NOT used heavily at all by my standards.

I threw it in the garbage and am debating if I should fish it out and try and get warranty service. (supposedly there is a one year warranty on this thing). I just went through HELL and back getting a warranty replacement on a convection oven from a mfr with customer service in my state (cost only 11 dollars to ship the thing back to them) it took about 3 months to get a replacement. These people, I have no idea where to start. I will update if I go for warranty service.

Otherwise, have to say AVOID. Really moderate use and nothing heavy. Motor should not have given out, that knocking is bearing, not some plastic gear. I know a bit about motors and this just stank (and does stink)

UPDATE: I first emailed the Mfrs customer service in China, after several days without a reply I went to Amazon as time was growing short on that mfr warranty. At first, they gave me the same Mfr email in China and even suggested I call them (kidding? No, I don't think they were) I don't speak Mandarin and was not going to spend on an intl call to find out if they have any customer service there that speak English. I then asked Amazon about contacting the vendor instead. Well Amazon sent an email to vendor with the order number and said customer doesn't know what to do with item. Huh? Excuse me, in this case the Amazon customer service was worse English than what I ultimately got in China. Well, I then sent my own email to Vendor explaining that I do know how to operate it and was for 11 months until it conked out. I waited two days without a reply and then picked up a better known model on "well known online auction site". Now here is the truth, no sooner did I complete my purchase there than there is an email from vendor (I believe also in China) saying they will check into it. Another day they say they contacted mfr and have decided to send me a new one. Another day and they ask me to verify mailing address, tells me it takes about 1 to 2 weeks fedex from China and they would get back to me with a tracking number. A week went by and I heard nothing until yesterday they email me to say that tracking says I wasn't home (apparently they sent it needing a signature). Ok, left a note for Fedex and now have two grinders. My replacement will probably go in the garage as a spare since the other I purchased is a more powerful, better rated one. But you never know. I have not tried it yet, have not tried even the one I purchased but I figure between the two of them I should be covered. Not the first time I have ended up with two of something just like this happened, it did with a convection oven also.

Moral of story is it pays to be persistent about warranty service/replacement if it doesn't cost too much to ship back or if they don't ask for the broken item. But it can take awhile. I would like to give them two and half stars since they did replace it but you can't give halves so will go with three. It did last nearly a year and for a cheap one that isn't bad, though again, it was not pushed hard or often at all.
